crosswalks.label: Software Developers
crosswalks.rationale: Software Developers ground graphics software implementation, performance and hardware/software interaction but do not isolate rendering pipelines or GPU-specific evidence.

crosswalks.label: Special Effects Artists and Animators
crosswalks.rationale: Special Effects Artists and Animators provide adjacent visual-production evidence that helps preserve the distinction between renderer engineering and visual/art authorship.

findings.summary: O*NET software work grounds implementation/performance while adjacent visual-production work confirms that graphics engineering intersects but does not own authored visual/art outcomes.
method_labels: O*NET 31.0 Software Developer and Special Effects Artist occupational comparison
findings.rationale: The body narrows the software baseline into renderer/shader/artifact/performance machinery and explicitly retains art-direction boundaries.

findings.summary: Renderer correctness/performance evidence must remain distinct from aesthetic, asset-authoring and gameplay-readability judgment even when the same rendered artifact is shared.
findings.rationale: The crosswalk spans technical and artistic occupations, making the professional boundary essential to reusable execution.

gaps_against_body.description: Make generated render, visual technical inspection, aesthetic/art-direction judgment and gameplay/accessibility readability separate evidence/ownership surfaces.

nonclaims: This packet does not claim complete reconstruction of Graphics Engineer.
Software Developer and Special Effects Artist mappings remain partial/adjacent rather than profession identity.
No aesthetic quality, gameplay readability, hardware universality, TEST, WORKING or CANON claim is created.

high_stakes.authorization_nonclaim: This packet grants no art-direction, gameplay, accessibility, hardware/platform or institutional authority.
